biography.plain_text: Kerry Packer was an Australian media proprietor who inherited Australian Consolidated Press from his father, Sir Frank, and greatly expanded the family business. Born in Sydney, he became the country's richest man. His best-known deal was selling the Nine Network to Alan Bond, then regaining control after its buyer ran into trouble.

long_biography.plain_text:
When cricket authorities refused television rights to media owner Kerry Packer, he organised his own competition. World Series Cricket recruited leading international players and challenged the established game in 1977. Coloured clothing, floodlights and innovations in coverage helped reshape how cricket reached its audience. Two years later, the dispute ended with Packer securing the rights he had sought.

He applied similar ambition to golf. Hiring Jack Nicklaus to redesign the Australian Golf Club course, he also paid leading overseas players to compete in a revamped Australian Open. He secured exclusive television rights for several Australian golf tournaments.
